deck_title: Kepler-Noether equal-area angular momentum vs naive constant-omega orbit rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic Johannes Kepler (1609, Astronomia Nova) Second Law of equal areas in equal times & Emmy Noether (1918) SO(2) rotational symmetry angular-momentum conservation (dA/dt = 0.5 * r^2 * theta_dot = L/(2m) = const, scaling angular speed inversely with squared radius theta_dot(u) = omega_0 * r_0^2 / r^2 = omega_0 / (1 + u) to lock swept-area rate at A_dot/A_dot0 = 1.0000x across all 17 moment-of-inertia stations u in [0.0000, 1.0000] with 0/17 violated stations) versus naive uniform angular-velocity parameterization (theta(t) = omega_0 * t, which inflates swept-area rate and angular momentum as r^2/r_0^2 = 1 + u up to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at apoapsis u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-sector triangle-fan area quadrature.

cards.headline: Exact controls are useful; realism remains a separate job.
good_fit: Elliptical planetary/comet orbits, figure-skater spin-ups (pulling arms in), and Rankine/free-vortex particle swirls
Enforcing Kepler Second Law dA/dt = 0.5 * r^2 * dtheta/dt = const so satellites whip rapidly through periapsis and linger slowly at apoapsis
Conserving Noether SO(2) angular momentum L = I * omega across time-varying moment of inertia I(t)
Zero-drift angular update dtheta = (L / (m * dot(r, r))) * dt
not_for: Rigid turntable platters driven by a geared synchronous motor where every radius is forced to rotate at constant omega
